advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the out-of-band-seeded /rebar/prod/jira-api-token was created as a SecureString (matching the rebar_secrets type) so the adopting import applies cleanly with no type-change diff.
evidence: ABSENCE: the commit message states the three were 'seeded OUT OF BAND by an operator via the AWS CLI' but neither the message nor ssm.tf records the SSM type the operator used for jira-api-token, so a String-vs-SecureString mismatch at import time is unverified.
advisory.finding: The `jira-api-token` import block adopts the operator-seeded parameter into the `rebar_secrets` resource, which declares `type = "SecureString"`. If the operator seeded that parameter out of band as a plain `String` (the actual `put-parameter` command/type is not shown or asserted anywhere), the first adopting `terraform apply` will detect a type mismatch and attempt to change the parameter type, which can force replacement or fail — a drift/blast-radius risk on a live credential slot.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Document that /rebar/prod/jira-project is terraform-owned (value-managed, no ignore_changes) so operators know not to edit it out of band and expect it to stick.
evidence: ssm.tf:156-164: `resource "aws_ssm_parameter" "jira_project" { name = "/rebar/prod/jira-project" type = "String" value = "REB" tags = {...} }` — note no `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [value] }`
ssm.tf:97-99: sibling secret/plain resources all carry `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [value] }`
rebar.toml:78: `project = "REB"` confirms the value matches the drift-guard test
advisory.finding: The `jira_project` SSM parameter is fully terraform-managed with a real value (`REB`) and NO `ignore_changes`, unlike every other /rebar/prod param. This is intentional single-sourcing, but it means any operator who ever adjusts /rebar/prod/jira-project out of band will have it silently reverted to `REB` on the next apply — worth an explicit operator-facing note in the runbook so the divergence from the ignore_changes convention is not surprising.
